Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our call, I wanted to put a single note outlining a potential pilot structure that could help Aptitude ramp headcount and inference capacity ahead of your product launch while simplifying your next renewal. High level proposal: 

- 12-month pilot term (pilot counts toward renewal)
- Accelerated onramp: 3-month step-up schedule (20% / 40% / 40% of committed capacity) to match your expected traffic curve
- Upfront onboarding credit to offset early usage overage during month 1 (one-time credit)
- Auto-extend clause that renews the committed capacity for subsequent 12-month term unless customer opts out with 30 days notice
- Option to co-term to calendar July if you prefer alignment with other vendors

Attached is a short term-sheet that frames the numbers and mechanics (proposed-pilot-term-sheet.pdf). Can you confirm: 1) procurement contact to loop in (if different than this thread), 2) whether an auto-extend with 30-day opt-out is acceptable, and 3) any billing cadence preferences (monthly vs quarterly vs annual prepay)?

If it helps, we can lock in the currently quoted unit pricing for the pilot if you sign the term-sheet by March 16. Would love to set a short 30-minute call next week to walk procurement through the steps.

Thanks —

--
Soojin Lee

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the concise outline. A few quick clarifying questions from our side: 

1) Can the pilot be structured so that billing is quarterly in arrears? We prefer not to prepay for small startups.
2) On the auto-extend: what happens to unused committed capacity if we don’t consume our ramped volumes in months 2-3? Is there a carry-forward or credit mechanism?
3) We may want co-terming to July as you suggested — is there any pro-rata adjustment to the price if we co-term mid-year?

Looping procurement on the thread (procurement@aptitudelabs.com) — they’ll drive the SOW/PO cadence. We’re happy to do a short sync with your finance/legal.

Soojin —

Happy to take this. High level finance/legal guidance below (I’ll loop legal if we get to contract redlines):

- Billing cadence: We can offer quarterly-in-arrears for the pilot but will request a two-week deposit for month 1 to cover the accelerated ramp. That deposit is refundable/credit against the first invoice. It keeps cash risk low for them and predictable for us.
- Unused committed capacity during the ramp: we do not want unlimited carry-forward in a pilot. Recommend a one-time adjust/credit model: if they under-consume in months 2-3 relative to the step-up schedule, we provide a one-time usage credit equal to the difference up to 15% of the committed volume. Anything beyond that would be treated as standard overage (pay-as-you-go).
- Auto-extend: 12-month auto-extend with 30-day opt-out is acceptable; legal prefers we add language that auto-extended term renews at the then-current published unit rates unless customer and Redwood agree otherwise. Avoid perpetual carry-forward clauses.
- Co-term to July: Pro-rata adjustment is straightforward — we amortize the remaining value of the pilot across the new co-term; no price change if they co-term within 60 days of the pilot end.

I’ll draft a one-page finance note and attach it. If you want, I can also produce a short redline for the proposed term-sheet.

Thanks —

--
Kimberly Park
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Hi Emma / procurement —

Thanks for the questions and for looping procurement. Quick consolidated plan from Redwood that maps to Emma’s asks: 

1) Billing: we can do quarterly-in-arrears. We’ll request a refundable two-week deposit to cover month-1 accelerated capacity. Deposit will appear on the first invoice as a credit.
2) Unused capacity during ramp: we’ll apply a one-time usage credit up to 15% of the committed capacity if they under-consume in months 2-3; additional shortfall billed as overage at pay-as-you-go rates.
3) Auto-extend & co-term: we will include the 12-month auto-extend with a 30-day opt-out. If Aptitude chooses to co-term to July mid-contract, we will amortize any remaining credits pro-rata; unit pricing remains fixed for signings completed by March 16 per Soojin’s note.
